proposal.status: NEW proposal for explicit Director disposition; not a claimed existing grant or application of the unfinished review
proposal.common: A disclosure adapter belongs to the original source/event and applies identically whether or not anyone owns a Fate permission. Resolve it after the complete original RNG operation, before eligible rerolls and consequences. It changes no dice, timing, number of draws, resource cost, target set or seed. It provides an authorized event handle and the exact original component IDs/faces only to its named audience. Server-only seed/state, undisclosed targets, modifiers and source causes remain private. Authorized replacement results use the same audience and component scope; they create no second original disclosure event. A player controlling several bodies does not grant each body another body’s perception, range, hand or Reaction. No disclosure adapter overrides an actual source protection.

ownDeclaredAttack.sourceScope: An actual player-controlled character’s deliberately declared ordinary weapon, natural, unarmed or spell attack against a creature/object it actually perceives, under the original attack source. Includes actual Arcane Ray catalog /spells/402. Excludes another body’s attack, autonomous companion attacks, unknown-location/blind-fire attempts, secret attacks, nonattack checks/saves and automatic results. A distinct source-specific policy would be required for those.
ownDeclaredAttack.audience: Only the controller of the actual attacking character; not allies, enemies or an observing Coin holder merely because they see the attacker.
ownDeclaredAttack.generator: The actual attacking body, retaining the original source’s special origin where expressly applicable; this adapter grants no new spatial origin.
ownDeclaredAttack.disclosure: Complete original attack d20 component faces and IDs, die size, and effective higher/lower/ordinary selection mode. Show the full actual one- or two-d20 procedure; never a favorable subset. Do not reveal target AC, hidden flat modifiers, undisclosed sources or their identities, hit/miss or damage consequences before their normal checkpoint.
ownDeclaredAttack.explicitInformationChoice: This intentionally makes the effective d20 procedure of the actor’s own declared perceived-target attack visible even when an underlying cause of advantage/disadvantage remains undisclosed. Effective selection mode is a newly permitted narrow gameplay fact; cause/identity remains private. This is a consequential NEW choice for GPT to approve or replace, not an inference from camera visibility. It must be rejected/restricted explicitly if the game requires effective advantage state itself to remain secret.
ownDeclaredAttack.noAdditionalAccess: Having this readout supplies no reroll by itself. All actual Mark Omen, Fate Coin or Fate Reversal permission/cost/guard/Reaction/source predicates still apply.

ownBurningHands.sourceScope: Only actual Burning Hands /spells/426 with its original 15ft cone, DEX-save factor and one shared 3d6 pool; no extension to other fire spells, other damage pools, loot or generation RNG.
ownBurningHands.audience: Only the actual original caster’s controller.
ownBurningHands.generator: Actual original caster body, not an arbitrary recipient or UI animation.
ownBurningHands.disclosure: The complete shared three d6 component IDs and faces, with their ordinary summed raw pool, after the real pool is generated and before any recipient damage consequences. Every actual recipient still uses that same final shared pool with its own save/defenses.
ownBurningHands.eventExistence: Do not add a roll when the original source does not generate one. This grant requires at least one actual eligible cone recipient already independently perceived/known to this caster at resolution; otherwise this adapter grants no event handle or component readout. The response must not disclose whether additional hidden recipients exist, their number, identities, saves, defenses, eligibility or outcomes. One known recipient is sufficient irrespective of hidden-recipient count.
ownBurningHands.otherObservers: An outside holder H has no grant from this adapter; N02’s old observer-positive branch stays conditional. A new own-caster fixture is provided instead.

affectedConfusionController.sourceScope: Only the operative proposed Confusion behavior d4, nonempty target-selection 1dN and direction d8 at that affected body’s actually authorized opportunity; both printed school modes keep their actual access.
affectedConfusionController.audience: Only the controller retaining decisions for the affected creature T. Confusion’s caster and outside Coin holders gain nothing merely by perceiving T.
affectedConfusionController.generator: The affected T body at its actual behavior opportunity. No caster-location substitution.
affectedConfusionController.disclosure: Expose the completed d4 face before executing its branch. For a branch that actually calls for a later d8 or nonempty 1dN, expose that completed result before its movement/target consequence. Each is a distinct original event. For 1dN, show only the already-perceived legal candidate bodies and stable component-to-candidate mapping; never include unperceived U. Empty set creates neither draw nor reroll offer. Direction shows only the source’s fixed eight-direction mapping, no route/hidden-hazard data.
affectedConfusionController.reaction: Confusion itself retains target-controlled Bonus Actions/Reactions and creates no general Reaction prohibition. T can use its own existing Coin with usable hand and actual available Reaction if all source predicates pass; prior spending, actual Incapacitated or another prohibition still blocks use. No extra refresh, compelled Coin spending or new physical item is supplied.
affectedConfusionController.guard: Using Coin on d4 consumes its actual item/Reaction and that event’s guard; it does not automatically fund or grant another use on the separate later dN/d8 event. The normal actual resource limits still apply.

proposal.remainingClosed: No other source obtains a digital disclosure grant here. Positive outside-observer/save/check cases remain explicitly conditional composition tests until their own original source policy is authored. Negative hidden/total-only tests remain valid. These narrow adapters do not claim exhaustive presentation coverage of every eligible Fate source.
